notes: Read SKILL.md and references/details.md in full. The skill gives React Native/Expo architecture guidance: project layout, Expo Router navigation, an auth provider using expo-secure-store, offline-first React Query persistence, native modules (haptics, biometrics, push notifications), platform-specific styling, FlashList performance, and EAS build/submit/update.

Medium: the Quick Start has the agent scaffold a project with `npx create-expo-app@latest` and install npm packages with `npx expo install` (SKILL.md:51-59), and the EAS section lists `eas build`, `eas submit` to the App Store/Play Store and `eas update --branch production` OTA releases (details.md:557-569), which act on the user's Expo account. Acceptable because these are the standard Expo workflow for the user's own app; store submission and production OTA updates should only be run when the user explicitly asks.

eas.json uses placeholder Apple ID and ASC app ID and references a local google-services.json service-account key path (details.md:548-552); keep that file out of version control. Auth tokens are stored in SecureStore, which is the recommended pattern.
